title: Astrid and the Wreck
premise: Bush pilot Orsen Dunmore, hiding from a past she paid dearly to bury, pulls a sealed chest from a wrecked floatplane in a remote river — and finds it stamped with the seal of Vessland, a nation erased from every map. Inside are documents proving the 'accident' that killed expedition pilot Astrid Vale was murder, ordered by the same consortium that once owned Orsen's silence and now hunts the chest to bury the last witness. Forced to ferry a salvage crew who don't know what they're really looking for, Orsen must choose between the loyalty she owes the crew who trust her and the truth that could free her. In the end she burns her false papers, delivers Astrid's testimony to a Vessland exile court, and finally flies under her own name.
about_author: Sable Ishikawa is the pen name of a former floatplane dispatcher turned novelist who grew up in river towns where everyone had a reason to be far from home. Their work explores the quiet violence of small communities and the maps people draw to hide from themselves.

chapters.title: Fuel, Weather, Rumors
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establish her run: medicine, mail, and gossip upriver, her debts to fixer Halloran, and her practiced anonymity. A passenger mentions a salvage outfit asking about a plane lost twenty years ago. Emotional beat: the unease of a woman whose careful invisibility has begun to itch.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Low water exposes a wing in a back channel. She dives and hauls up a chest stamped with the Vessland seal, plus a waterlogged logbook signed A. Vale. Emotional beat: dread curdling into fascination — the river has handed her a past she thought was drowned.

chapters.title: The Name on the Logbook
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, night at her cabin. She dries the pages: Astrid Vale's entries describe being followed, a cargo she was ordered to dump, and a final entry cut mid-sentence. Orsen recognizes the consortium's courier mark — the same one that once bought her silence. Beat: recognition and fear.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The salvage crew arrives: leader Ivar Lund, a courteous man with a consortium retainer; young diver Petra, who idolizes Orsen; and surveyor Dek, who watches everything. They charter her — to find the wreck she's already found. Beat: Orsen's double life begins, guilt already taking root.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with a Halloran scene. Halloran reveals the consortium holds her debt and offers to clear it if she reports what the crew finds. Refusal has a price he names plainly. Beat: the trap closing — her loyalty is a commodity someone else already sold.

chapters.title: Up the Kettle River
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The expedition flies into the interior; a storm forces a rough landing and the crew bonds over repairs, Petra confessing why she dives. Orsen nearly tells them about the chest and doesn't. Beat: belonging, and how much it costs to lie to people being kind to you.

chapters.title: Petra's Hands
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, first shift. Diving the wreck, she finds tool marks on the fuselage — deliberate sabotage — and a second, empty crate slot. She reports it to Ivar, who goes strangely quiet. Beat: the discovery that this was never a salvage job.

chapters.title: Ivar's Retainer
chapters.summary: Ivar's POV. Flashback-tinged: he took consortium money to confirm the chest's location and destroy its contents, believing the job was routine reputation-management. Now he suspects he's the deniable part of a murder cover-up. Beat: a decent man realizing his loyalty was purchased.

chapters.title: Halloran's Message
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A supply flight brings a coded note: the consortium knows the chest is found; deliver it or the crew becomes collateral. Orsen hides it, plans to run the chest out alone at night. Beat: isolation deepening — she chooses the lie that protects everyone and saves no one.

chapters.title: The Night Flight
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She attempts a solo pre-dawn extraction with the chest; Dek, sleepless, catches her loading and says nothing — just watches. Fog forces her back. Beat: the plan failing, and the first crack in her conviction that secrecy is safety.

chapters.title: Astrid's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Deciphering the water-damaged final pages, she learns Astrid was carrying evidence that would have restored Vessland's stolen borders — and that the consortium's pilot who shot her down was a man Orsen once flew for. Beat: the past and present colliding; her silence was complicity all along.

chapters.title: Dek's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dek's POV. He reveals to Orsen he's not a surveyor but an exile-court investigator hunting Astrid's testimony for twenty years. He offers her a choice: testify, or hand over the chest and stay invisible. Beat: the truth finally offered as a door, not a weapon.

chapters.title: The Crew Meeting
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Orsen's POV. Orsen confesses everything — the chest, the logbook, her debt, her false name. Petra feels betrayed; Ivar admits his retainer; the crew fractures. Beat: the painful arithmetic of loyalty versus truth, played out around a camp stove.

chapters.title: Halloran Arrives
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Halloran lands with two consortium men and a court order claiming the salvage. He offers Orsen her debt cleared and her old name erased, again. She asks for one night to comply. Beat: the devil's offer, made politely, with the crew as hostages to fortune.

chapters.title: What Petra Dives For
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra dives one last time and recovers Astrid's sealed personal case — a letter to a daughter, and the original documents, hidden where the consortium's divers never looked. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the dead pilot gets her voice back.

chapters.title: The Split
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The crew votes: Ivar will stall Halloran with the empty chest; Dek, Petra, and Orsen will fly the real evidence out through the storm front. Orsen realizes she's flying toward exposure, not away from it — and wants to. Beat: commitment; fear chosen willingly.

chapters.title: Storm Crossing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flight sequence. The crossing nearly kills them: ice on the wings, a failing radio, Halloran's charter shadowing them. Petra navigates by Astrid's logbook route notes — the dead pilot guiding them home. Beat: terror, trust, and the crew becoming a crew.

chapters.title: The Forced Landing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They put down on a frozen lake short of the exile court's seat; Halloran's men arrive by ground. Ivar, arriving unexpectedly, stands between them and buys time with his retainer contract's fine print. Beat: loyalty repaid in kind — Ivar choosing the crew over his paymaster.

chapters.title: Halloran's Truth
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, confrontation on the ice. Orsen offers Halloran the one thing he fears: testimony that he was the courier who sold out Astrid. His men waver; the debt dissolves not by payment but by exposure. Beat: the climax — truth wielded not as confession but as leverage.

chapters.title: The Exile Court
chapters.summary: Dek's POV. In a borrowed hall, Astrid's documents are read into the record; Vessland's erased borders enter testimony. Orsen testifies under her true name — spoken aloud for the first time in a decade. Beat: catharsis; identity reclaimed at the cost of every hiding place.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Upriver
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The consortium's reach is broken in the territory; Halloran is gone; Ivar takes the salvage outfit honest. Orsen repaints her plane's registration with her real name. Beat: quiet reckoning — belonging earned, not performed.

chapters.title: Astrid and the Wreck
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, closing. She flies Astrid's daughter to the lake where the plane still lies, and they leave flowers on the water. Orsen finally reads the letter meant for her, kept all these years in a chest the river gave up. Final beat: the wreck was never the plane — it was the life Orsen buried, now surfaced and forgiven.
